newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Bashir in S.Africa to talk peace for Sudan.
newsitem.headline: Bashir in S.Africa to talk peace for Sudan.

text.p: Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir arrived in South Africa on Monday night ahead of delicate talks with President Nelson Mandela on ways to end a 14-year civil war in southern Sudan, officials said.

"Yes, he (Bashir) has arrived. He has no official arrangements tonight," a South African Foreign Affairs official told Reuters, adding that the Sudanese president was expected to meet Mandela on Tuesday morning.
The official said talks would take place in Pretoria and had been scheduled provisionally for 0900 GMT.
A news briefing was expected to follow the talks in the afternoon.

Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, who has recently met delegations from the conflicting sides in the Sudan, would also send a special envoy to Pretoria for the talks, the Foreign Affairs department said in a statement.
The envoy, who was not identified, would be at the meeting "in support of finding an acceptable and lasting solution to the problem", the statement said. It gave no further details.
Mandela has played the role of peace broker several times since he emerged in 1990 from over a quarter-of-a-century in jail to lead South Africa from apartheid to democracy.

Alone or in concert with other southern African leaders, he has contributed to peacemaking missions in Angola, Algeria, Lesotho, Swaziland, Burundi, Nigeria and Zaire, which is now known as the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
In the Sudan, Mandela has attempted over the past few months to help mediate in the fighting which has pitted Christian and animist rebels in the south against the Moslem, Arab north.

The Pretoria government said Bashir's visit came at Mandela's request and took place against the background of an African initiative under the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), chaired by Kenyan leader Daniel Arap Moi.

"President Mandela and the South African government fully support and encourage all parties to the conflict in Sudan to participate constructively in the IGAD initiative," the Foreign Affairs statement said.

John Garang, leader of the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army, has already held talks with Mandela on ways to end the war. Pretoria's Foreign Affairs Department confirmed on Monday that they met in South Africa in December 1996.
